note: Rewritten from Ahmad 1965, original in English (Termites (Isoptera) of Thailand, Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History 131: 1–113). The specimens were collected by M. Ahmad on 1962-03-29 from a termite mound. This entry contains only the two soldier castes (major and minor soldier): the alate and the worker are not described in the original; the minor-soldier measurements are not tabulated separately, and only the major soldier has the six measurements of Table 8. Fig. 31 (major soldier head, pronotum, mesonotum and metanotum in dorsal view, head in lateral view, labrum, mandibles, postmentum, antenna) and fig. 32 (minor soldier) are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the key it is separated from the other species, whose postmentum is widest in the distal half, by the postmentum being widest in its posterior half; in the major soldier of this species the anterior third of the postmentum is constricted, the basal third is widest, and the lateral margins bulge distinctly over the basal half.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier (fig. 31): head reddish brown, the anterolateral corners slightly darker; labrum and antennae brown; mandibles dark brown with the base slightly paler; pronotum brown, tinged with red; mesonotum, metanotum and abdominal tergites rusty yellow; legs pale brown. Head hairs very sparse: a pair of setae on the anterior margin of the postclypeus and another pair somewhat farther behind the fontanelle; a row of 4 setae on each lateral margin of the labrum, with 2 long and 2 short setae on the transparent tip; 2 setae on the postmentum in front of the waist; hairs on the pronotum very sparse, with a few microtrichia on the anterior margin and a pair of setae on the posterior half; the mesonotum and metanotum each have a pair of backward-directed setae. The head narrows anteriorly, widest slightly below the middle, slightly concave at the middle at the level of the compound eyes; the fontanelle is minute and circular, situated slightly in front of the middle. The anteclypeus is membranous and far wider than long. The labrum is broad and dome-shaped, widest over its anterior half; the tip is transparent and triangular. The mandibles are long and stout, moderately incurved at the tip; the base of the left mandible has several fine serrations; the right mandible has none. The postmentum is arched, constricted over its anterior third, widest over its basal third; the lateral margins bulge distinctly over the basal half. The antennae have 17 segments; segment 3 is nearly twice as long as segment 2; segment 4 is shorter than segment 3 and slightly longer than segment 5. The pronotum is much narrower than the head, with an indistinct T-shaped median mark; the middle of the anterior margin is convex with a shallow but distinct median notch; the lateral lobes project and are narrowly rounded; the posterior margin is concave. The mesonotum is narrower than the pronotum; its lateral lobes are angular; its posterior margin is concave. The metanotum is slightly wider than the mesonotum; its lateral lobes are angular; the middle of its posterior margin is shallowly concave. Minor soldier (fig. 32): head brownish yellow; labrum and antennae brown; mandibles reddish brown with the base paler; pronotum pale brown; legs straw yellow; abdominal tergites pale brown. Head hairs sparse; the labrum has a row of setae on the sides of the transparent tip; the pronotum has a few setae along the margins. The head is shaped like that of the major soldier; the fontanelle is minute and circular, situated slightly in front of the middle. The compound eyes are small and nearly circular. The sides of the labrum are convex and widest in the middle; the tip is transparent and nearly triangular. The mandibles are long and slender, slightly curved at the tip; the base of the left mandible has several fine serrations; the right mandible has none. The postmentum is strongly arched, about twice its maximum width, widest over its posterior half, with the waist in the anterior half. The antennae have 17 segments; segment 3 is slightly longer than segments 2 and 4; segment 5 is shorter than segment 4. The pronotum is narrower than the head; its anterior margin is convex and raised with an indistinct notch; the lateral lobes project and are narrowly rounded; the posterior margin is concave; the mesonotum is slightly narrower than the pronotum. Measurements (mm, six major soldiers, holotype / range / mean): head length to the lateral base of the mandibles 4.03 / 3.88—4.03 / 3.97; head width to the lateral base of the mandibles 2.01 / 1.94—2.16 / 2.02; head width at the posterior ends of the antennal carinae 2.55 / 2.44—2.73 / 2.59; maximum head width 3.20 / 3.02—3.31 / 3.21; length of the left mandible 2.02 / 2.01—2.08 / 2.04; postmentum length 2.70 / 2.37—2.73 / 2.56; postmentum width before the constriction 0.93 / 0.86—0.93 / 0.88; postmentum width at the constriction 0.72 / 0.67—0.72 / 0.69; width of the posterior half of the postmentum 0.95 / 0.93—0.97 / 0.94; pronotum length 1.15 / 1.08—1.15 / 1.10; pronotum width 2.39 / 2.27—2.39 / 2.31; mesonotum width 2.08 / 1.83—2.11 / 1.99; metanotum width 2.16 / 2.01—2.17 / 2.11.
